**Integration steps**

**Step 1 — Get authorization.**

 Obtain an OAuth2 bearer token with your
API credentials and send it as `Authorization: Bearer {access_token}`
on every call. Obtain a fresh token before it expires — an expired
token is rejected before the signature is even checked.

**Step 2 — Sign the payload.**

 Build the canonical string
`merchantTill|timestamp|nonce` (pipe-joined, no whitespace) and
compute the lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256 digest of it, keyed with your
signing secret. Generate `timestamp` and `nonce` fresh for every
request, including retries.

    import hmac, hashlib, uuid
    from datetime import datetime, timezone

    # Your credentials
    signing_secret = "<your_signing_secret_key>"
    till_value = "<your_merchantTill_value>"

    # Generate fresh values for each request
    timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    nonce = str(uuid.uuid4()).lower()

    # Build and sign
    signing_string = f"{till_value}|{timestamp}|{nonce}"
    signature = hmac.new(
        signing_secret.encode("utf-8"),
        signing_string.encode("utf-8"),
        hashlib.sha256
    ).hexdigest()

    # Add to requestParameters:
    # "timestamp": timestamp, "nonce": nonce, "signature": signature

Sandbox till number (merchantTill) and signing secret are issued to
you on the Developer Portal — use those values in place of the
placeholders above, and never commit a secret key to source control
or ship it in client-side code. Your production secret key is
available on the Merchant Portal; your production till number is
the one registered with LOOP for your merchant account. The same
signing secret is used across all payment endpoints for a given
till — you do not need a different key per endpoint.

**Step 3 — Build the request body.**

 Assemble the service envelope
(`serviceCode`, `txnReference`, `requestParameters`) with the
signed `timestamp`, `nonce` and `signature` nested inside
`requestParameters` alongside `merchantTill`, `merchantRcvTill`,
`accountNumber`, `amount` and `channel` (fixed at `LOOP`). See
ProcessPayToMpesaTillRequest below. `merchantRcvTill` is the M-Pesa
buy-goods till number you are paying to — for a LOOP merchant till
use Pay to LOOP Till instead, or Pay to M-Pesa Paybill for a
paybill business number.

    {
      "serviceCode": "MRCHNT_PAYMENTS",
      "txnReference": "e9f0a1b2-c3d4-5678-ef01-345678901234",
      "requestParameters": {
        "merchantTill": "133239",
        "merchantRcvTill": "247247",
        "amount": "350",
        "channel": "MPESATILL",
        "timestamp": "2026-08-07T10:30:00Z",
        "nonce": "e5f6a7b8-c9d0-1234-efab-345678901234",
        "signature": "f8b3c2d1e0a5..."
      }
    }

**Step 4 — Send the request.**

 POST the signed body with your bearer
token to `/services/process-request`.

**Step 5 — Read the response.**

This endpoint is fully synchronous —
there is no callback. HTTP 200 confirms the gateway accepted the
request; check `data.serviceTransactionStatus` (COMPLETED, PENDING
or FAILED) and `responseDetails.rspCode` (`OGW00000` means the
payment was confirmed) to determine the actual outcome before
considering the payment settled. See the statusCode table on the
200 response below for handled-failure codes.

**Step 6 — Handle failures and retries.**

 On any 400/401 statusCode,
correct the payload or your credentials before retrying — resending
it unchanged fails the same way. See the statusCode table on the
200 response below for the full set of causes and resolutions.

**Step 7 — Test in sandbox, then go live.**

Sandbox till number and
signing secret are issued on the Developer Portal for testing; do
not use them in production. Production credentials (secret key and
till number) are available on the Merchant Portal once your
integration is approved — everything else about the contract stays
the same.

response.name:
The gateway returns HTTP 200 for essentially every outcome, success or handled failure — branch on the `statusCode` field inside the response body, not the HTTP status line:

| statusCode | Cause | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Success | The payment was accepted; check `data.serviceTransactionStatus` and `responseDetails.rspCode` for the actual outcome. There is no callback for this endpoint. |
| 400 | Timestamp is expired or set in the future. | Generate a fresh UTC timestamp at the time of the request. |
| 400 | Nonce has already been used. | Generate a new unique nonce for every request — never reuse one, even on retry. |
| 400 | Signing fields are at the request root instead of inside requestParameters. | Move timestamp, nonce and signature into the requestParameters object. |
| 400 | A required field is missing or has an invalid value. | Review all required parameters and ensure values match the expected format. |
| 401 | Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired. | Generate a fresh token from the authorization endpoint and retry. |
| 401 | Signature verification failed. | Check the signing string order (merchantTill, then timestamp, then nonce), confirm the correct secret key is used, and verify hex encoding. |

data is an empty object `{}` on every non-200 statusCode.

description.content: Added as a part of security scheme: oauth2

Pay to M-Pesa Till — pay directly from your LOOP till to an M-Pesa buy
goods till. You provide the till number, a reference, and the amount —
the equivalent of scanning a till for a buy-goods payment, initiated
programmatically from your system. The call is fully synchronous —
there is no callback for this endpoint; check the response directly
for the outcome. See the Integration steps in the operation
description below.
